You write the application; `backd` serves it. This section covers every feature an application uses, in roughly the order you meet them:

| I want to… | Go to |
|---|---|
| Describe my data: schemas, indexes, realms | [Configuration](configuration/) |
| Read, write and query documents over HTTP | [HTTP API](api/) |
| Users, sessions, sign-in providers, API keys, access rules | [Authentication](auth/) |
| Group a customer's users and documents | [Organizations](organizations/) |
| Server-side logic: calls, jobs, cron, webhooks, email | [Functions](functions/) |
| Attachments, uploads, downloads, sharing | [Files](files/) |
| Reach users' devices | [Push](push/) |
| Talk to it from JavaScript or Dart, or generate clients and types | [Clients](clients/) |
| See a complete application | [Examples](examples/) |

Running the service itself — deployment, providers, administration — lives in [Operate](../operate/).
